subject: NeuroLytics dedicated onramp: proof-of-performance (PoP) sizing and swap schedule
messages:
From: Alana Reed <alana@neurolytics.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.inference>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 28 Nov 2028 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated onramp — load profile & PoP request

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week. The execs want a short proof-of-performance (PoP) to validate cost/latency at our 95th percentile before we sign the reserved capacity commitment. Summary of what we saw on hosted:
- Peak qps: ~42 requests/s (model mix: 60% text-gen, 30% chat-stream, 10% embeddings)
- Typical prompt length: 180 tokens; responses average ~220 tokens

Can Redwood run a 48-hour validation on a dedicated pool sized for 1.5x expected 95th qps and provide per-token latency P50/P95, KV cache hit rate, and cost delta vs hosted? Procurement also needs an initial swap window that doesn’t overlap our month-end processing window (we’re blocked 6th–8th each month).

I attached our required PoP criteria doc (neurolytics_pop_test_plan.xlsx). Let us know available dates — we’re targeting an onramp in early December if performance lines up.

—Alana
Head of Product, NeuroLytics
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.inference>
To: Alana Reed <alana@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated onramp — load profile & PoP request

Alana —

Appreciate the clear profile and the PoP doc. We can run the 48-hour validation; preliminary sizing recommendation is a 6-GPU reserved slab (A100-class equivalent) with the following rationale:
- 1.5x headroom on 95th qps to account for burst patterns
- Continuous KV cache enabled to capture prefix reuse (we expect 18–22% token savings)
- Batch configuration: adaptive batching with 8–16 concurrency targets to preserve P95 latency

Karthik, Marissa — can you confirm ops availability to stand up the dedicated pool the week of Dec 3? NeuroLytics asked to avoid Dec 6–8 windows. If we do a dry-run PoP starting Dec 4 (48h), swap back or finalize by Dec 6 morning so they are clear for their month-end.

We’ll generate a short PoP report with P50/P95 histograms, cost per 1,000 tokens vs hosted, and suggested quantization profile if some tail latency is above target.

Priya
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 30 Nov 2028 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated onramp — ops & sizing checklist

Quick ops check from runtime side:
- We can provision a 6-GPU cohort in us-west-2 with the requested kernel mix. Expected throughput baseline: 45–48 qps at 95th for the stated model mix with adaptive batching.
- KV cache warm-up: plan for a 4–6 hour warm-up during the PoP to reach steady hit-rate numbers.
- Observability: we’ll enable token-level tracing and cost breakdown for the PoP. Need the NeuroLytics traffic replay file or representative curl load generator.

Ben — I’ll need one SRE for swap window on Dec 4 (start 09:00 PT) and coverage on Dec 6 (06:00 PT) for a possible rollback. Marissa — can you draft the PoP report template (P50/P95 tables, cost delta, quantization notes, suggested ops follow-ups)?

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
From: Alana Reed <alana@neurolytics.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Cc: NeuroLytics Procurement <procurement@neurolytics.ai>
Date: Fri, 01 Dec 2028 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated onramp — load profile & PoP request

Thanks — attached is a small replay bundle (7.2k requests, representative distribution) and our procurement guardrails. We can shift the PoP to start Dec 4 at 09:00 PT. Dec 6 morning rollback window is fine; we’ll keep Dec 6–8 blocked internally for month-end but OK to finalize before 06:00 PT.

Procurement: we’ll expect a short statement of work that defines the reserved slab, billing start/end conditions for the PoP, and acceptance criteria.

—Alana
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.inference>
To: Alana Reed <alana@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated onramp — PoP confirmed / swap plan and deliverables

Alana / team —

Summary and next steps (confirmed):
- PoP start: Dec 4, 09:00 PT (48 hours). Dedicated slab: 6 GPUs (us-west-2).
- Deliverables: PoP report (P50/P95 latency by API route, token-level cost comparison vs hosted, KV cache hit-rate, recommended quantization/profile knobs). Report will be shared 24h after PoP completes (Dec 6, ~09:30 PT).
- Swap window/rollback: finalization by Dec 6 05:30–06:30 PT; ops will revert if any regression above agreed thresholds.
- Acceptance criteria (from NeuroLytics doc): P95 latency <= 1.8x hosted P95 and cost per 1k tokens <= hosted cost * 1.25.

Attachments: swap-window-dd-mm.pdf (swap runbook + rollback checklist). Ben — you’re primary SRE for the swap; Karthik — runtime monitoring hooks; Marissa — PoP report template. I’ll coordinate with procurement on the SoW and billing hold for the PoP.

Thanks — we’ll be on call for the Dec 4 start.

Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0147
Attachments: swap-window-dd-mm.pdf (runbook), neurolytics_pop_test_plan.xlsx (provided by customer)
